thread:
Sam (sec): FYI upstream published a cluster of CVEs that touch FlashAttention kernels, protobuf, and sentencepiece.
Sam (sec): Reported details: CVE-2025-1001 (FlashAttention OOB read), CVE-2025-1002 (protobuf unsafe deserialization), CVE-2025-1003 (sentencepiece buffer overflow). Affects vLLM/Triton stacks on dedicated pools and some private installs.
Rachael (eng-runtime): Ack. Can you paste links? I want to see exploitability notes.
Sam (sec): Links in sec-ticket: https://secure/edge/CVE-2025-1001, https://secure/edge/CVE-2025-1002, https://secure/edge/CVE-2025-1003
Sam (sec): Quick read — protobuf is the highest-risk (remote deserialization), FlashAttention is local OOB but workable exploit in some configs, sentencepiece lower but non-zero.
Li (ml): For vLLM/Triton: we use patched protobuf in hosted API, but Dedicated pools may still run older wheel. We should inventory wheel versions across clusters.
Tom (oncall): I can run a quick inventory script on dedicated nodes.
Tom (oncall): deploy-bot triggered an automated scan earlier — shows 24 nodes with protobuf 3.12.x and flash 1.2.0 kernels.
deploy-bot: scan report: https://ci/reports/inventory/1965432100
Rachael (eng-runtime): Suggested immediate mitigations:
- Block public ingress to affected inference routes (if any customer-facing) — short term.
- Force fallback to CPU-backed kernel or disable FlashAttention fastpath with env FLAG_DISABLE_FAST_KERNELS=1.
- Pin protobuf to patched 3.20.5+ in our runtime images and ship hotpatch to Dedicated.
Sam (sec): Prioritization proposal: 1) protobuf (CVE-1002) — patch rollouts + audit log check for suspicious deserializations, 2) FlashAttention (CVE-1001) — kernel update + disable fast kernels for high-risk pools, 3) sentencepiece (CVE-1003) — backport patch where used.
Li (ml): Agree. Also need to run prompt evals after protobuf upgrade — tokenization/deserialization differences sometimes break cached KV keys.
Rachael (eng-runtime): Rollout plan:
- Create canary on a single dedicated pool (non-prod) with protobuf pinned & FLAG_DISABLE_FAST_KERNELS=1.
- Watch latency + failure rates for 2 hours.
- If green, push to remaining Dedicated in waves (10%/30%/100%).
- For Private/VPC customers, publish advisory + backport instructions; offer support window.
Sam (sec): KMS stuff: if we need to rotate keys (e.g., for image signing or secrets), coordinate with ops. Rotating key aliases will require updating creds in Private packages; ensure audit logging around key change is ON.
Tom (oncall): I'll add an entry to the oncall checklist: on rotation, run smoke tests and reconcile with config-sync. Also ensure RBAC change: only sec-admins can push kernel flags to prod pools.
Rachael (eng-runtime): Can we do hotpatch without restarts? For protobuf wheel upgrade we'll need rolling restarts of workers. For FlashAttention flag we can env-swap on orchestration side and reload processes.
Sam (sec): Also: enable verbose audit logs for inference routes for the next 72h. Tag entries with 'cve-2025-1002-obs'.
Li (ml): I'll run a small corpus fuzz against sentencepiece and FlashAttention hooks on canary cluster — want to validate patched behavior.
Rachael (eng-runtime): CI action items:
- infra: build runtime images with protobuf 3.20.5+ and flashattention 1.2.1+ backports.
- eng-ml: run eval suite for regressions.
- sec: prepare customer advisory draft.
Sam (sec): Incident handling: open incident INC-2025-2100, set severity to P2 for now, escalate to P1 if exploits seen. Coordinate with SOC for IDS signatures.
Tom (oncall): Oncall -> will be primary comms and runbook executor during rollout window.
Rachael (eng-runtime): I'll start the canary at 1965432160. Pushing images now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-dedicated-pool at 1965432165
Rachael (eng-runtime): Canary live. Flag set, pinned protobuf. Monitoring.
Li (ml): Fuzz run started against canary.
Tom (oncall): Monitoring dashboards: no auth anomalies, small latency bump +1.2% — within threshold.
Sam (sec): Good. Keep audit logs and escalate on any suspicious deserialization failure or unknown KMS ops.
Rachael (eng-runtime): If canary is green at +2h, proceed to 10% wave.
Sam (sec): I'll draft advisory and customer guidance for Private deployments — include KMS rotation checklist, RBAC note: require sec-admin approval for kernel flag toggles.
Rachael (eng-runtime): Thanks team. Will update thread with rollout status.
Tom (oncall): Updating INC-2025-2100 with timestamps and actions.
Sam (sec): :white_check_mark:
